source_text: Tunc attentantur numerosis durisque cruciatibus per stationarium militem, iustorum piorumque carnificem, adhibitis in auxilium crudelitatis eius centurione et Cirtensium magistratibus. Hoc est diaboli sacerdotibus, tanquam membrorum laceratione frangeretur fides, cui cura corporis uilis est. Et Iacobus quidem, sicuti erat in uirtute fidei semper austerior, qui et infestationes iam semel Decianae persecutionis euicerat, affectauit se non Christianum tantum, sed et diaconum confiteri. Marianum autem tormentis fecit obnoxium, quod se lectorem tantum, sicuti fuerat, fatebatur. Quaenam illa tormenta! Quam noua, quam diaboli uenenato sensu et deiciendi artibus exquisita supplicia! Pependit Marianus ad uulnera, eoque martyri etiam in ipsis lacerationibus suis affuit gratia, sic torsus est, ut illum exaltaret et poena. Nexus autem qui pendentem gerebant, non manus, sed summos apices pollicum uinxerant, scilicet ut digitorum tenuis exilitas plus in ferendis membris ceteris laboraret. Addita etiam pedibus iniusta pondera, ut dum discordantibus poenis utrimque distracta et uiscerum conuulsione resoluta, de neruis suis totius corporis compago penderet. Nihil egisti iuxta dei templum, iuxta Christi coheredem, nequitia gentilis. Suspenderis licet membra, concusseris latera, diuulseris uiscera, Marianus noster in deum fidens, quantum corpore, tantum et mente crescebat. Uicta denique feritate torquentium, rursus in carcerem de triumpho suo multum laetatus includitur. Ibi cum Iacobo et ceteris fratribus gaudium uictoriae dominicae frequenti oratione celebrauit.
thought_title: Hanging torture endured and defeated in prison triumph
orientation: Marian and James have been dragged to Cirta and put in prison, and the narrator now describes their examination by torture.
pass_a_gloss: Then they are tried with numerous and harsh tortures by means of a soldier on station, an executioner of just and holy men, with a centurion and the magistrates of the people of Cirta brought in to aid his cruelty. This is the way of priests of the devil, as if faith, to which care for the body is cheap, could be broken by mangling of limbs. And James indeed, just as he was always sterner in strength of faith, who also had already once overcome the attacks of the Decian persecution, eagerly sought to confess himself not only a Christian but also a deacon. But it made Marian liable to torments, because he confessed himself only a reader, just as he had been. What torments those were. How new, how exquisite punishments sought out by the poisoned mind of the devil and by his arts of casting down. Marian hung toward wounds, and grace was present to the martyr even in his own manglings, he was so twisted that even punishment lifted him high. Moreover the bonds that carried him as he hung had bound not his hands, but the topmost tips of his thumbs, namely so that the thin slenderness of his fingers would labor more in bearing the rest of his limbs. And unjust weights were also added to his feet, so that while torn apart on both sides by disagreeing pains and loosened by wrenching of his inward parts, the framework of his whole body hung from its own sinews. You accomplished nothing next to the temple of God, next to the coheir of Christ, pagan wickedness. Though you hang his limbs, shake his sides, tear apart his inward parts, our Marian trusting in God was growing as much in mind as in body. Finally with the savagery of his torturers conquered, he is shut again into prison rejoicing greatly over his triumph. There with James and the other brothers he celebrated the joy of the victory that belongs to the Lord with frequent prayer.

soldier on station or guard duty
framework or joining of a body

choices.why: keeps military function and hostile moral label from the brief, not a neutral rank

pass_b_english: Then they were put to many hard tortures by a soldier on station, an executioner of just and holy men, with a centurion and the magistrates of Cirta lending their help to his cruelty. They were the devil's priests, as if tearing limbs could break a faith that holds the body cheap.

James, who had always been sterner in the strength of his faith and had already once lived through the attacks of the Decian persecution, volunteered to confess himself not only a Christian but also a deacon. Marian, because he confessed himself only a reader, as he truly was, was left exposed to the tortures. What tortures those were! How strange they were, how cunningly devised by the devil's poisoned mind to drag men down!

Marian hung to be wounded, and grace stayed with the martyr even amid his torn flesh, so that the twisting lifted him high through pain. The cords that held his hanging body bound not his hands but the very tips of his thumbs, so that the thin slightness of his fingers would labor harder in bearing all the rest. Unjust weights were hung from his feet as well, so that, pulled apart on both sides by clashing pains and loosened by the wrenching of his entrails, the whole frame of his body hung from its sinews. You achieved nothing, pagan wickedness, against God's temple, against Christ's coheir. You may hang his limbs, shake his sides, and tear his entrails; our Marian, trusting in God, grew as much in mind as in body. At last the torturers' savagery was beaten, and he was shut back in prison, rejoicing greatly in his triumph. There with James and the other brothers he celebrated with constant prayer the joy of the victory that belongs to the Lord.
